messages:
Diego: FYI — getting multiple customer escalations about p95/p99 spikes after last night's runtime change. They see p99 jump to ~2.3s from ~420ms on generation workloads. No 5xxs, just much higher tail latency.

Carla: Which change did we roll yesterday? I was on the deploy but missed the final merge.

Ben: We merged the new attention kernel selector + FlashAttention2 compile flags into the release candidate. Default policy switched to \"auto\" which prefers FlashAttn for eligible ops.

Alice: Oh. Did the selector start picking SDPA fallback for some sequence lengths? That can tank perf if kernels aren't optimized for hybrid paths.

Diego: Logs from a customer host attached below — see the kernel select trace: 
```
kernel_selector: FLASHATTN_v2 chosen for layer 4
kernel_selector: FLASHATTN_v2 chosen for layer 5
kernel_selector: fallback_to SDPA_SCALAR for layer 6 (seq_len=2048)
kernel_selector: SDPA_SCALAR executed, kernel_time_ms=1800
```
They hit fallback mid-run which causes a big tail.

Emma: Do we have profiler traces? Need to confirm if it's GPU kernel time or something else (IO/queueing).

Diego: Attached perf dump from their run (snipped): 
```
GPU utilization: 92%\nKernel 1 (flash): 12ms\nKernel 2 (flash): 14ms\nKernel fallback (sdpa_scalar): 1800ms\nBatch size: 1\nKV cache hits: 0\n```
So it's definitely kernel-level.

Ben: That matches a known edge: if sequence length crosses our tested threshold the selector sends to SDPA_SCALAR which is a safe-but-slow fallback when FlashAttn kernels don't match shape. The new compiler flags changed how some ops are fused which altered the shape heuristics.

Carla: Is it regressing only on long seqs? customer reported typical prompt lengths ~900 then in the session a system message + history pushed it above 1500.

Alice: Repro steps we used locally:
1) curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -d '{"model":"rwd-gpt-medium","input":"<900 token prompt> + long history"}'
2) observe p95/p99 with --sequence 1500
It reproduces for me on a dev node when I force attention_mode=auto.

Diego: Can we flip attention_mode to sdpa on the affected pool as a mitigation? That should be slower on short seqs but avoids the pathological fallback.

Emma: Two-tier approach: immediate mitigation = set per-pool override to prefer SDPA (runtime flag). Medium-term = tune selector thresholds and add a specialized FlashAttn kernel path for the sequence shapes hitting fallback.

Ben: Commands to flip per-host config (use admin API):
```
# set per-node preference to sdpa
curl -X PATCH https://admin.redwood.internal/nodes/<node-id>/tuning \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <admin-token>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"attention_mode":"sdpa"}'
```
This will apply immediately to the node's runtime.

deploy-bot: Starting rolling config change to pool \"gen-large\" (50 hosts) — patch in flight.

Emma: I pushed that to the canary group (5 hosts) and saw p99 drop from ~2.1s to ~480ms. Canary looks good. Rolling to remaining hosts now.

Diego: Good call. Who's owning the kernel selector fix? We should avoid manual toggles for long.

Ben: I'll own the selector tuning. First step: add a shape-aware unit test matrix that includes the customer's sequence shape (n_head/n_kv/seq_len combos) and validate we pick the fast path. Also adding a fallback guard that logs excessive kernel_time and auto-favors the other kernel if the fallback is long — short-circuit for tail protection.

Carla: Is there any risk toggling sdpa for everyone? We need to check cost impact. Ben, can you quantify token-cost delta?

Ben: Quick estimate: sdpa path is ~1.5x token-cost for medium seqs in terms of GPU time. For this pool traffic it's a small % of total spend vs having unhappy customers; recommend targeted pool override for affected customers and short-term global override only if needed.

Diego: Support notes for CS: please tell affected customers we have a mitigation in place (per-pool override) and we're working on a long-term kernel selector fix. Ask them for recent examples (request ids) and approximate session lengths.

Carla: I'll coordinate with Support. Diego, can you drop a list of affected customer IDs into the ticket?

Diego: Done — added customer ids: cust-742, cust-1991, cust-88. Included one sample request-id: req_202603150914_abc123.

Alice: For the build-side remediation: revert the compile flag default to keep old heuristics while we add better tests. Quick patch: set -DENABLE_FLASHATTN_DEFAULT=0 in the runtime build, then trigger a canary builddeploy. That avoids touching runtime configs.

Ben: I'll prepare the patch and the regression test. Also adding a perf alert: p99 delta > 2x for a model pool triggers an automated investigation run that collects kernel traces.

deploy-bot: Canary rollback to release abc123 initiated (jobs queued).

Emma: Postmortem items:
- Improve kernel selector unit/integration tests (Ben)
- Add runtime safety heuristics to prefer non-fallback path if fallback kernel_time > threshold (Ben)
- Add perf regression alerting tied to deploys (Emma)
- Document admin API tuning steps for Support (Carla)

Diego: Thanks everyone. Keep this thread updated with canary results and when the selector patch lands. Current status: mitigation rolled to pool -> stable as of +12m; ongoing work to recompile/revert flags and add tests.

Carla: Noted. I'll send CS the update and mark the ticket as \"mitigated (perf override)\". :thumbsup:

Ben: Leaving a TODO in repo: tests/perf/selector_shapes.yaml with customer shapes. I'll PR within the hour.

Emma: Once Ben's fix is in, let's schedule a weekend canary to validate at scale before toggling the default back to auto.

Diego: Closing loop — will follow up with a short incident summary for the incidents channel after we finish the rollback/patch.

infra-bot: Alert suppressed for p99 spike on gen-large pool after override applied.

Carla: Thanks — good triage.
